data.narrative:
Atomic Machines is a Series A semiconductor company that has raised $144M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 3 public semiconductor comps (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in chips and semiconductors, with primary focus on 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables: Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and Positron AI ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression uses the $144M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $288M. Peer-median anchoring applies the median valuation of three same-sector peers at $2.0B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comp anchoring does not apply; while public semiconductor peers trade at a median 20.4x price-to-sales, Atomic Machines' revenue is not disclosed, precluding multiples-based valuation.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $245M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.1B. The gap between stage-progression ($288M) and peer-median ($2.0B) reflects tension between capital-deployed methodology and market comparables. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to named peers, product commercialization timeline, and whether the target commands a premium or discount within the $1.0B–$2.3B range occupied by Rebellions, d-Matrix, and Positron AI.
